what_this_measures: Whether the removed surface the audit view exists to show is actually visible from the camera that ships, rather than merely inside the frame. One ray from the camera eye per area-weighted sample of the removed surface, against the meshes the view draws.
why_in_frame_was_not_enough: camera_framing_probe.py reports the worst point of each view in units of the frame half-extent, and the audit view was clean by that measure. It draws the retained surface in the same pane, so a sample can sit at reach 0.3 and be entirely behind opaque geometry. That is the failure the source's own VIEW_GEOMETRY comment names -- an audit view that looks like the audit happened -- reached by a mechanism the comment's fix does not address.
what_changed: /world/mesh is hidden by default in this view, through the same table that gives the view its contents and its camera geometry. It is still carried and one click away. The fused cloud stays visible: points occlude nothing a ray can hit, so the overlay is still shown against the observations it is judged against.
the_residual_this_does_not_fix: The removed surface occludes itself. It is an extrapolated shell, so from any single eye the far side of it sits behind the near side, which is the whole remaining loss after this change and is not something a visibility default or a camera can recover. An orbiting reviewer sees the rest; a single static frame does not.

reproducibility.why_seeded: The armadillo scene resamples a complete mesh, and Open3D seeds a global generator rather than a call. Unseeded, the first two runs of this harness reported 38.5% and then 38.0% -- small enough to read as noise and really an unseeded draw.
reproducibility.and_still_not_bit_exact: Seeding does not make this reproduce exactly, and claiming it would be wrong. The largest deviation observed in the visible fractions is 7.9e-05, across 6 runs, recorded with its run count in occlusion-repeat-spread.json. An earlier version of this record said 2e-5 and called it agreement: that came from two runs, and a reviewer's own two runs exceeded it before their numbers were compared against this record at all. Two observations give a sample minimum, not a bound. Triangle counts move by a few of 1.09M on the eagle and a few tens of 1.04M on the armadillo, with the kept and removed counts moving by the same amount in opposite directions: triangles sitting within floating-point reach of the crop limit changing which side they land on. orient_normals_consistent_tangent_plane is multithreaded and its tie-breaking is not seeded, so a seed cannot remove this. The barycentric sample count moves with them and is not evidence of anything further: it is exactly 6 * removed_triangles in every run measured. The synthetic controls are exactly identical across runs, re-verified over all 6, which locates the variation in the reconstruction rather than in the measurement.
reproducibility.why_it_does_not_affect_the_verdict: The gate is 50% and the measured values are 78% and 82%, so a 7.9e-05 wobble is 3 orders of magnitude below the margin. It is recorded because a figure republished to the last digit would otherwise look falsified on the next run -- which is what happened: a reviewer ran the harness and the figure they got differed, exactly as this note exists to predict.

the_recorded_camera_is_bound_to_the_prod.the_weakness: test_the_harness_uses_the_product_camera_rather_than_its_own was named for the right property and did not enforce it. It asserted camera_elevation_degrees > 0.0, which 35.0 satisfies -- and 35.0 is the synthetic control eye already present in this harness. Review changed the recorded 28.0 to 35.0 and the suite still passed 11 of 11. camera_eye was checked with len(...) == 3. The other three assertions were over harness source text, which cannot substantiate what the harness did.
the_recorded_camera_is_bound_to_the_prod.it_was_a_guard_weakness_not_a_false_numb: Review confirmed independently that the harness does call the product's _view_cameras() and take cameras[REMOVED_VIEW], so the recorded 28.0 was correct. What was missing was anything that would keep it correct.
what_binds_it_now: the recorded angle equals CAMERA_ELEVATION_DEGREES, imported from the product rather than copied as a literal
the elevation is recovered from the eye's own geometry, so the recorded angle cannot be edited on its own

the eye's whole direction from its look target equals the direction the product fits, obtained by calling the product's own _camera() on throwaway points rather than by reimplementing its formula. The offset depends only on up and the constant, never on the geometry, so any point set returns it -- a unit tetrahedron and a larger offset box agree to nine decimals.

fields_added_for_it.camera_look_target: the centre the product fitted the eye around
fields_added_for_it.camera_up: the up vector it fitted against
fields_added_for_it.no_measured_value_moved: The fit is deterministic given the same geometry, so these were added by recomputing only the camera and checking the recomputed eye against the recorded one. Max drift was 0.0 in both scenes, so the target and up provably belong to the same fit and nothing measured was re-run.

mutations_each_verified_applied.mutation: one scene's up tilted, the other left alone
review's own forgery: both eyes invented, both at exactly 28 degrees
mutations_each_verified_applied.note: passed 11 of 11 against the elevation-only binding

mutations_each_verified_applied.mutation: both eyes moved to 10x distance, direction preserved

the_recorded_camera_is_bound_to_the_prod.where_this_note_lives: At the top level, not under `controls`. I put it there first and test_the_instrument_reports_both_extremes failed on a KeyError: every entry under `controls` is a calibration control that must carry samples_behind_eye == 0, or its zero could be a clipping result. A guard note has no samples, so it does not belong in a section reserved for things that were measured.

a_claim_of_mine_review_falsified.what_i_wrote: that two scenes agreeing on the recovered elevation could not both be hand-written, because the direction depends only on the constant and up
a_claim_of_mine_review_falsified.how_it_fell: Review replaced both eyes with invented ones chosen to sit at exactly 28 degrees, about a thousand units out on a different azimuth, and the suite passed 11 of 11. Two forgeries agree perfectly whenever the forger knows the constant, and the constant is in the source. The two-scene check proved that the angle and the eye are consistent with each other and with the constant -- real, and it closed the original finding -- but not that the eye is the one _view_cameras() produced.
a_claim_of_mine_review_falsified.closed_rather_than_reworded: Review asked only for the sentence to be corrected, judging the full eye unbindable from a CPU-only test. The azimuth turned out to be bindable: it is geometry-independent, so the product's own _camera() yields it without open3d. Review's two forged eyes are 0.62 away from the product's direction and now fail.

what_is_still_not_bound.the_distance_along_that_direction: Solving it needs the point geometry -- it is fitted so the widest actual sample sits just inside the frame -- which is why the direction is what gets bound. Measured rather than reasoned: moving both eyes to 10x their distance along the correct direction still passes 11 of 11.
what_is_still_not_bound.why_this_is_stated: The previous version of this note claimed more than it could support, and a reviewer falsified it with a call rather than an argument.
